Rafael Camara: Haas confirm Brazilian will race in final two rounds of F1 season rather than chase F2 championship
Rafael Camara will race again for Haas at the Qatar Grand Prix and Abu Dhabi Grand Prix ahead of joining full-time for the 2027 season; Camara leads the Formula 2 standings but will not feature in the final rounds
Sunday 22 November 2026 18:48, UK
Haas have confirmed that Rafael Camara will continue to feature for the team in the final two races of the season, rather than challenge for the Formula 2 championship.
Camara made his debut at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix earlier this month, following Esteban Ocon's departure ahead of the Mexico City Grand Prix and reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa stepping in for that race.
He also raced alongside team-mate Ollie Bearman at the Las Vegas GP, finishing 16th, with the Brazilian now retaining his place for the remainder of the season.

The 21-year-old will feature at the Qatar GP from November 27-29 and the Abu Dhabi GP the following week, ahead of taking up a full-time seat with Haas from next season.
In a statement, Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said: "We're excited to be able to finish the season with Rafa driving and building on his first two race starts with the team in Brazil and America.
"I'm delighted that Rafa's embraced every track session as a learning opportunity and embedded himself further within the team.
"We now get to finish the season together, which is advantageous to us all ahead of a relatively short off-season and as our 2027 preparations get under way."
Camara leads the F2 standings by seven points over Red Bull reserve Nikola Tsolov ahead of the final two rounds of the season, although would be unable to compete in both events on the same weekend.
Invicta Racing, Camara's F2 team, shared on X: "What a journey it's been Thank you for everything Rafa and best of luck for the rest of the @f1 season with @haasf1team."
For Camara to claim the F2 title, a year on from winning the Formula 3 championship, he would need Tsolov to score less than seven points from the final four races and no other driver to move above him in the standings.
Formula 1 heads to the Middle East for the final two races of the season, with live coverage from the Qatar Grand Prix from Friday on Sky Sports F1 ahead of the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix in December. Stream Sky Sports with NOW.
